subject: Request: Security Subsidy & Audit Window for Encrypted VPC Evaluation
messages:
From: Alice Sandoval <alice.sandoval@securemed.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@securemed.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:07:05-07:00
Subject: Encrypted VPC evaluation — subsidy & audit window request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking the initial call yesterday. As discussed, SecureMed is preparing a 5–8 week isolated evaluation of an encrypted VPC deployment for a clinical data ingestion workflow. To move forward we need confirmation of two things from Redwood: (1) a security-linked subsidy (trial credits) to cover inference costs for the POC, and (2) a narrow audit window where your team will perform a quick configuration review and evidence collection (SOC/TLS/keys) before we begin ingesting PHI-like test data.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our POC requirements and timeline (securemed_poc_requirements.xlsx). High-level asks: 30k token credits (estimate), a 6-week sandbox with increased retention for logs during the audit, and a signed MOU describing data handling and escrows.

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood will require (SOC 2 report version, encryption-at-rest attestation, KMS integration steps) and whether we can get the subsidy and audit window approved in the next 72 hours? Procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Alice Sandoval
Senior IT Program Manager
SecureMed
[Attachment: securemed_poc_requirements.xlsx]

From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Alice Sandoval <alice.sandoval@securemed.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T10:12:20-07:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted VPC evaluation — subsidy & audit window request

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear summary + spreadsheet.

Quick answers up front: we can typically sponsor a security-linked subsidy for isolated VPC evaluations and arrange a configuration/audit window, but approvals depend on a short set of controls and the MOU. To keep things moving I need:

- A point of contact for your security lead (name + email) so we can coordinate the evidence checklist.
- Confirmation that no PHI will be included in the initial ingest (test/pseudonymized only) until the audit window closes.
- Signed non-binding MOU (I attached our standard outline) specifying scope, credits, and data handling.

I attached an outline of our security-eval process and a draft MOU for subsidy requests (redwood-security-eval-outline.pdf, redwood-mou-subsidy-2026.docx). If you can return the signed MOU and the security POC requirements by EOD tomorrow we can route for expedited approval.

Proposed expedited path (if approved):
- Redwood provides a conditional subsidy of token credits (up to 40k) and a 6-week isolated VPC sandbox.
- We schedule a 90-minute audit window (configuration review + evidence transfer) during week 0.
- Formal MOU + DocuSign signature to follow.

Looping in Jonas (security ops) and Marissa (sales lead) to expedite approvals — Jonas, any immediate red flags? Marissa, should I route this to sales ops or billing?

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Partner
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-security-eval-outline.pdf, redwood-mou-subsidy-2026.docx]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Alice Sandoval <alice.sandoval@securemed.com>, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted VPC evaluation — subsidy & audit window request

Hi Alice and team — thanks for the details, Irene. Small follow-up from Security Ops side.

We can approve a conditional subsidy up to 35k token credits for the evaluation, with the following conditions to mitigate compliance risk:

1) SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) or equivalent audit evidence uploaded to our secure intake link prior to the audit window.
2) Encryption attestation for customer-managed KMS (or confirmation that Redwood-managed KMS will not store customer keys for the POC).
3) A 90-minute configuration review call in week 0 where SecureMed shares IAM/ingest patterns and we verify network controls.
4) A written acceptance of Redwood's temporary log-retention policy for the sandbox period (we will extend retention only for the audit window and purge logs after the agreed date).

If these conditions are met we will:
- Issue the subsidy (35k tokens) and spin up an isolated VPC sandbox for 6 weeks.
- Provide a checklist and a short remediation plan if we identify any issues.

Marissa — please create a HubSpot opportunity under D-2026-SEC-9427 and route to Finance for a temporary subsidy code (expires +8 weeks from activation). Alice — I'll send the secure intake link and a proposed time for the week 0 review; please confirm your security contact.

Jonas Weber
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/D-2026-SEC-9427]

From: Alice Sandoval <alice.sandoval@securemed.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@securemed.com
Date: 2026-09-15T09:01:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Encrypted VPC evaluation — subsidy & audit window request

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our internal expectations.

Security contact: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@securemed.com> (copied in procurement separately). We will upload our SOC 2 Type II and the encryption attestation to the secure intake link once Jonas shares it.

One operational note: procurement is asking if the evaluation can be extended to 8 weeks (procurement timeline + scheduled maintenance windows). Are you able to grant a one-time extension at the finance level, pending no-major-findings after week 4? I attached a soft PO stub for internal reference (securemed_procurement_po_stub.pdf).

If you can confirm the intake link + a possible 2-week extension option, we will sign the MOU and move forward.

Best,
Alice Sandoval
Senior IT Program Manager
SecureMed
[Attachment: securemed_procurement_po_stub.pdf]
